prompt: A panoramic laboratory-and-compute scene shows thousands of uncoiled DNA helices rendered as four-letter A-C-G-T text strings streaming from stacked genome libraries into a glowing neural-network “chatbot” labeled Evo1/Evo2; the model emits statistically similar but novel sequences while a thought-bubble robot merely predicts letter co-occurrence without biological insight. Those synthetic strings become physical DNA pipetted into living cells under a microscope that splits into a functional virus versus an inert molecule, proving wet-lab testing is required. Surrounding icons of other genome types, locked data vaults, access-control gates, and DNA-order screening machines sit beside arguing scientists, visually encoding the open questions of training data, users, and safeguards.
